new_task_1.title: Honor falsey callable objects as attribute converters
new_task_1.description: The 24.3.0 upgrade fixes attrs field conversion so callable converter objects are recognized even when they evaluate false in boolean contexts. Only `None` should mean that no converter was configured.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that attrs applies configured field converters based on whether a converter is present, not on the converter object's truthiness, so falsey callable converter instances still run during initialization.

expectation.grounded: When an attrs field declares a converter with a callable object, the generated initialization path must treat any non-`None` converter as active. Callable instances that implement conversion through `__call__` but return `False` from `__bool__` must still be wrapped and invoked as converters. A field with `converter=None` must remain the only case treated as having no converter.
expectation.conceptual: User-defined converter objects should work because they are callable, not because they happen to be truthy. Falsey converter instances should behave the same as other configured converters.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the meaning of omitting a converter or explicitly passing `None`: those cases must still disable conversion. Existing behavior for ordinary truthy callable converters and existing `attr.Converter` instances must remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be narrowly scoped to converter detection so it removes an edge-case failure without changing normal converter semantics.

behavior: Attrs treats any non-`None` field converter as configured, even if the converter object is falsey.
A callable converter instance with custom `__bool__` returning `False` is still invoked during attribute conversion.
Passing `None` as the converter continues to mean that no conversion should occur.
Existing truthy callable converters and pre-wrapped `Converter` instances continue to behave as before.
acceptance_criteria: Given an attrs field configured with a callable object whose `__bool__` returns `False`, when an instance is created, then the field value should still be passed through that converter.
Given a falsey callable converter that transforms the input value, when initialization runs, then the stored attribute value should reflect the converted result rather than the original input.
Given a field with `converter=None`, when an instance is created, then attrs should continue to treat the field as having no converter.

Given existing code that uses ordinary callable converters or `attr.Converter` instances, when upgrading, then converter execution semantics should remain unchanged aside from the falsey-converter fix.
